from.title: How String::from works
from.description: Makes an owned, growable String from a string literal.

slides.caption: "hi" is a &str: fixed text stored in the program. String::from copies it into memory that s owns.
The characters are copied into a new buffer on the heap.
s owns that buffer: it can grow, change, and is freed when s goes out of scope.
"hi".to_string() and "hi".to_owned() do the same. Use &str to read text, String to own and change it.

push_str.title: How String::push_str works
push_str.description: Appends text to the end of the String.

title.text: let mut s = String::from("Hello"); s.push_str(", world");

slides.caption: s holds "Hello". push_str adds ", world" after it.
", world" is copied to the end. If there is not enough room, the buffer grows first.
push_str borrows its argument, so the text you append stays usable. s += ", world" does the same.
push takes a char (single quotes), not a string.
A char can take up to 4 bytes in the String; push encodes it as UTF-8.

pop.title: How String::pop works
pop.description: Removes and returns the last char.

note.text: a whole character, not a byte

slides.caption: pop takes the last character off the end.
'é' is the last character (2 bytes). Both bytes are removed together.
s is now "h". An empty String would give None.
pop never splits a character, even when it takes several bytes.

insert_str.title: How String::insert_str works
insert_str.description: Inserts text at a byte position; everything after it moves right.

title.text: let mut s = String::from("Hello!"); s.insert_str(5, " there");

slides.caption: insert_str(5, ...) puts the text before byte 5, which is the !.
" there" is inserted; the ! moves to the end.
The position is a byte index and must be on a character boundary, or it panics. insert(i, ch) inserts a single char.

remove.title: How String::remove works
remove.description: Removes and returns the char at a byte position.

slides.caption: remove(1) takes out the character that starts at byte 1.
'c' moves left to close the gap: s is "ac".
Like Vec::remove, this shifts everything after the removed character.

truncate.title: How String::truncate works
truncate.description: Shortens the String to a byte length.

slides.caption: truncate(2) keeps bytes 0 and 1 and drops the rest.
The length is in bytes and must be on a character boundary, or it panics.

retain.title: How String::retain works
retain.description: Keeps only the characters for which the closure returns true.

slides.caption: retain checks every char and removes the ones that fail.
The spaces fail the test: removed.
a, b and c pass and are kept, in order.
retain changes the String in place; s.chars().filter(..).collect::<String>() would make a new one.

split_off.title: How String::split_off works
split_off.description: Cuts the String at a byte position and returns the second half.

title.text: let mut s = String::from("Hello, world"); let w = s.split_off(7);

slides.caption: split_off(7) moves the bytes from 7 to the end into a new String.
Both Strings are independent afterwards. The position must be on a character boundary.

clear.title: How String::clear works
clear.description: Empties the String but keeps its memory.

slides.caption: clear removes all characters at once.
s is "", but its buffer is kept for new text.
Reusing one String with clear in a loop avoids allocating a new one each time.

as_str.title: How String::as_str works
as_str.description: Borrows the whole String as a &str.

title.text: let s = String::from("hi"); let r: &str = s.as_str();

slides.caption: Many functions take &str. as_str lends out the String's text without copying it.
r points at the same bytes that s owns.
While r is in use, s cannot be changed (it is borrowed).
Usually you do not need it: &s turns a &String into &str automatically where a &str is expected.

from_utf8.title: How String::from_utf8 works
from_utf8.description: Turns bytes into a String if they are valid UTF-8.

slides.caption: from_utf8 takes a Vec<u8> and checks that it is valid UTF-8 text.
104 is h and 105 is i: valid, so Ok("hi"). No copy is made.
A lone 255 is never valid UTF-8: Err, and you get your bytes back from the error.
String::from_utf8_lossy replaces invalid bytes with � instead of failing.

insert.title: How String::insert works
insert.description: Inserts one char at a byte position.

slides.caption: insert(1, 'e') puts e before the character at byte 1.
e is inserted; l, l, o shift right.
insert_str inserts a whole &str. The position must be a character boundary.

len.title: How String::len works
len.description: The number of bytes, not characters.

slides.caption: ñ needs 2 bytes in UTF-8; a and b need 1.
3 characters but len() is 4. chars().count() gives 3.

from_utf8_lossy.title: How String::from_utf8_lossy works
from_utf8_lossy.description: Turns bytes into text, replacing invalid bytes with �.

slides.caption: Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become the replacement character instead of an error.
It returns a Cow: no copy when all bytes were valid.

drain.title: How String::drain works
drain.description: Removes a byte range and gives it back as an iterator of chars.

note.text: s = "hello world": take the first word

slides.caption: The range is in bytes and must fall on character boundaries.

replace_range.title: How String::replace_range works
replace_range.description: Replaces a byte range with new text, in place.

title.text: let mut s = String::from("Hello, Bob"); s.replace_range(7.., "Ann");

slides.caption: replace_range swaps the text in a range for new text; the lengths can differ.
Unlike replace, it changes the String itself and works by position, not by pattern.

into_bytes.title: How String::into_bytes works
into_bytes.description: Turns the String into its Vec<u8>, without copying.

slides.caption: into_bytes hands over the String's buffer as a Vec of bytes.

extend.title: How String::extend works
extend.description: Appends every char (or &str) of an iterator.

slides.caption: extend pushes each item onto the end.
Works with any iterator of char or &str, like s.extend(words.iter().copied()).

string.title: How to_string works for String
string.description: Makes a copy of a String.

slides.caption: Calling to_string on a String clones it; both stay usable.
Prefer a.clone(): it says what happens. Pass &a when a borrow is enough.

new.title: How String::new works
new.description: An empty String, which does not allocate until text is added.

slides.caption: new() reserves no memory; the first push does.
String::with_capacity avoids reallocations when you know the size.

with_capacity.title: How String::with_capacity works
with_capacity.description: An empty String with room for n bytes reserved.

slides.caption: Building a long String piece by piece is faster when the room exists up front.
Capacity is in bytes, not characters.

capacity.title: How String::capacity works
capacity.description: How many bytes fit before the String must grow.

slides.caption: len counts used bytes; capacity counts available bytes.
shrink_to_fit gives the spare room back.

reserve.title: How String::reserve works
reserve.description: Makes room for at least n more bytes.

slides.caption: reserve may allocate more than asked, to make future growth cheap.
reserve_exact asks for no extra headroom.
After building a String, extra room can be returned.
Only worth it for big, long-lived Strings.

as_mut_str.title: How String::as_mut_str works
as_mut_str.description: Borrows the String as a &mut str.

slides.caption: A &mut str allows in-place changes that keep the length the same.

into_boxed_str.title: How String::into_boxed_str works
into_boxed_str.description: Turns the String into a Box<str>, dropping spare capacity.

slides.caption: Box<str> stores only a pointer and a length (16 bytes instead of 24).
The text now lives in a Box<str>.
Good for many small strings that never change.

from_utf16.title: How String::from_utf16 works
from_utf16.description: Decodes UTF-16 code units into a String.

slides.caption: Each u16 is a code unit; a lone surrogate is invalid.
0xD800 alone is an unpaired surrogate: Err.
from_utf16_lossy replaces bad units with � instead.

from_utf16_lossy.title: How String::from_utf16_lossy works
from_utf16_lossy.description: Decodes UTF-16, replacing invalid units with �.

slides.caption: Broken parts become the replacement character.
Use it when partial text is better than an error.

is_empty.title: How String::is_empty works
is_empty.description: true if the String has no bytes.

slides.caption: is_empty looks at the length only.

leak.title: How String::leak works
leak.description: Gives up the String forever and returns a &'static mut str.

slides.caption: For text computed once at start-up that must live for the whole program.
The String lets go of its buffer.
Each call leaks memory; never call it in a loop.

try_reserve.title: How String::try_reserve works
try_reserve.description: Reserves room, returning an error instead of aborting.

slides.caption: try_reserve lets a program survive an impossible allocation.

clone.title: How String::clone works
clone.description: A new String with a copy of the text.

slides.caption: The clone has its own buffer; changing it does not affect a.
Pass &a or &str when you only need to read the text.

from_iter.title: How String::from_iter works
from_iter.description: Builds a String from chars or string pieces; this is what collect() uses.

slides.caption: Every char (or &str) from the iterator is pushed onto a new String.

default.title: How String::default works
default.description: An empty String, used when a default value is needed.

slides.caption: The struct asks each field for its default.

from_string.title: How Vec<u8>::from(String) works
from_string.description: Turns a String into its bytes, without copying.

slides.caption: The String's buffer becomes the Vec.

box_str-from.title: How Box<str>::from(String) works
box_str-from.description: Turns a String into a Box<str>, dropping spare capacity.

slides.caption: A Box<str> is a little smaller and cannot grow.
The String gives up its spare room.

as_bytes.title: How String::as_bytes works
as_bytes.description: The String's UTF-8 bytes as a slice, without copying.

slides.caption: into_bytes() gives an owned Vec<u8> instead.

extend_from_within.title: How String::extend_from_within works
extend_from_within.description: Appends a copy of part of the String to its own end.

slides.caption: The range is in bytes and must fall on character boundaries.

reserve_exact.title: How String::reserve_exact works
reserve_exact.description: Makes room for exactly n more bytes.

slides.caption: For when you know the final size.
reserve may allocate more for future growth.

try_reserve_exact.title: How String::try_reserve_exact works
try_reserve_exact.description: Reserves exactly n more bytes, returning an error instead of aborting.

string_drain-as_str.title: How string::Drain::as_str works
string_drain-as_str.description: The part of the drained range not handed out yet.

title.text: let mut d = s.drain(..3); d.next(); d.as_str()

slides.caption: drain(..3) covers "abc"; after one next(), "bc" is left.
The rest is removed when the Drain is dropped.
The first byte is valid; 255 is not.
valid_up_to() tells how much is usable.

from_utf8_error-into_bytes.title: How FromUtf8Error::into_bytes works
from_utf8_error-into_bytes.description: Gets the original bytes back after a failed conversion.

slides.caption: from_utf8 took ownership of the Vec; the error hands it back.
Then try from_utf8_lossy, or report the problem.

from_utf8_error-as_bytes.title: How FromUtf8Error::as_bytes works
from_utf8_error-as_bytes.description: Looks at the bytes that failed to convert.

slides.caption: 0xC3 starts a two-byte character, but the second byte is missing.
into_bytes takes them back by value.

cow-from.title: How Cow<str>::from works
cow-from.description: Wraps a &str (borrowed) or a String (owned) in a Cow.

slides.caption: Functions can return either kind through one type.
Lets you avoid allocating when nothing needs changing.

cow-from_iter.title: How collect into Cow<str> works
cow-from_iter.description: Collects chars or strings into an owned Cow<str>.

slides.caption: Collecting always builds a new String inside.
Useful when the target type is fixed as Cow<str>.

from_utf8_unchecked.title: How String::from_utf8_unchecked works
from_utf8_unchecked.description: Makes a String from bytes without checking UTF-8 (unsafe).

slides.caption: Invalid UTF-8 here is undefined behaviour.

as_mut_vec.title: How String::as_mut_vec works
as_mut_vec.description: Mutable access to the String's bytes as a Vec<u8> (unsafe).

slides.caption: The String must stay valid UTF-8 when you are done.
push and push_str are the safe ways.

into_raw_parts.title: How String::into_raw_parts works
into_raw_parts.description: Splits a String into pointer, length and capacity, giving up ownership.

slides.caption: Forgetting to rebuild leaks the memory.

from_raw_parts.title: How String::from_raw_parts works
from_raw_parts.description: Rebuilds a String from pointer, length and capacity (unsafe).

slides.caption: The parts must come from a String (same allocator, valid UTF-8).
Errors on invalid units or an odd byte count.

from_utf16le_lossy.title: How String::from_utf16le_lossy works
from_utf16le_lossy.description: Decodes LE UTF-16 bytes, replacing invalid parts with �.

from_utf16be_lossy.title: How String::from_utf16be_lossy works
from_utf16be_lossy.description: Decodes BE UTF-16 bytes, replacing invalid parts with �.

slides.caption: An odd trailing byte also becomes �.
